subject: Logs life cycle — quick reference and customer actions
messages:
From: Elise Turner <elise.turner@brightbank.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@brightbank.com
Date: 2029-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick questions on default retention (requests vs outputs)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking this — a couple of follow-ups from our security review. Can you confirm the default retention windows for the hosted Redwood API for: (1) raw requests/prompts, (2) direct model outputs (generated text), and (3) derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking scores, indexes)? We also need to understand whether streaming chunks or KV cache fragments are persisted by default.

Two other items:
- If we request erasure for a session (session_id example: sb-ff22-9a), what is the expected end-to-end timeline to have all copies removed?
- Are there backups/replicas that could cause data to remain beyond the deletion window?

We're preparing an internal memo for compliance and would appreciate a short written summary we can include. If easier, happy to jump on a 20-minute call.

Best,
Elise Turner
Security & Risk — BrightBank

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Elise Turner <elise.turner@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, procurement@brightbank.com
Date: 2029-05-10T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on default retention (requests vs outputs)

Hi Elise — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact overview; Marissa from Security is looped in for the detailed bake-off. I've attached a short redaction checklist and an example session export to illustrate fields we purge vs preserve.

Summary (high level):
- Raw requests / prompts: stored by default for 21 days in hosted accounts (used for routing, debugging, and short-term quality checks).
- Model outputs (generated content): stored by default for 90 days; used for customer diagnostics and optional troubleshooting.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking indexes): retained by default for 365 days unless customer configures an earlier TTL or explicitly deletes the artifact.
- Streaming chunks: not persisted by default unless the customer enables "session recording" in their project config.
- KV cache: ephemeral by design; retained up to 12 hours and rotated per-instance — not part of long-term logs.

Deletion and backups:
- Customer-initiated deletion (via Support request or self-service API) triggers an erase workflow that typically completes within 72 hours for primary logs and up to 7 days to clear all replicas and caches.
- Backups are on a rolling window; we do not keep archived backups longer than 60 days unless a customer requests a legal hold.

Next steps:
1) Marissa, can you add any technical caveats (snapshots, third-party backups)?
2) Elise, if BrightBank wants a stricter default for your account we can propose per-account TTL overrides and document in the MSA.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
\Attachments: RB-redaction-checklist.pdf (pdf), example-session-export.json (json)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Elise Turner <elise.turner@brightbank.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-11T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on default retention (requests vs outputs)

Hi Elise — adding the technical details Jordan flagged. I'm pasting short Q&A plus runbook so your compliance team can copy into the memo.

Q: What counts as a stored "request" vs a "derived artifact"?
A: We treat the original HTTP payload (prompt text + metadata) as a request. Anything produced by the model (raw text, function call responses) is an output. When a customer elects to create searchable artifacts (embeddings, vector indexes) those are flagged as derived and tracked separately.

Q: Default retention windows (hosted):
- Requests/prompts: 21 days (default)
- Model outputs (per-response): 90 days (default)
- Derived artifacts (embeddings/indexes): 365 days (default)
- KV cache: ephemeral, up to 12 hours
- Streaming fragments: not stored unless "session recording" enabled

Q: Deletion workflow and timeline:
- Self-service erasure API: if you provide session_id or request ids, the call will queue the erase job. Primary data removal: usually within 24–72 hours. Replica/cascade removal (batches, caches, and in-flight analytics): up to 7 days.
- Support-assisted erasure (for legal/enterprise requests): we open a ticket and provide a timeline and proof-of-deletion report.

Q: Backups and snapshots:
A: Point-in-time snapshots may include copies of logs for disaster recovery. These snapshots are rotated and overwritten on a 60-day window by default. For EU-resident accounts we ensure snapshots are in-region unless the customer opts into cross-region replication.

Q: When is deletion irreversible?
A: Once the erase workflow reports "completed" and the proof-of-deletion is issued, primary stores and our retained replicas/snapshots (within the standard rotation window) no longer contain the data. If a snapshot was exported by the customer or shared externally, that copy is outside Redwood's deletion scope and must be handled by the recipient.

Runbook (recommended customer steps to ensure full removal):
1) Identify session_id(s) or dataset IDs.
2) Call the self-service erasure API (endpoint and sample payload in the linked doc).
3) Verify job status via the console / API; request proof-of-deletion JSON.
4) If any exports or manual downloads exist (e.g., from analytics or ops), notify recipients to purge their copies.

Notes & caveats:
- Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured with stricter TTLs or immediate erase hooks; this requires an MSA amendment for Dedicated or on-prem configuration for Private.
- If BrightBank requires sub-24-hour full erasure we can propose a custom SLA but it typically requires reserved capacity and configuration changes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
From: Elise Turner <elise.turner@brightbank.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-11T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on default retention (requests vs outputs)

Thanks Jordan & Marissa — this is helpful. Two quick clarifications: (1) You say backups rotate at 60 days — does that mean a deletion requested today may still be present in a snapshot for up to 60 days before rotation overwrites it? (2) For the proof-of-deletion, what fields are included in the report?

Also, can you confirm whether EU-resident logs remain in EU regions for both primary and backup stores (BrightBank requires in-region residency by default)?

Regards,
Elise
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Elise Turner <elise.turner@brightbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2029-05-12T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick questions on default retention (requests vs outputs)

Elise — quick answers to unblock your memo and procurement:

1) Backups: deletion does not retroactively remove data from an already-taken external export or a customer pull. For internal snapshots we maintain a rolling 60-day overwrite window. Practically, that means there is a potential for data to exist in a snapshot for up to 60 days after deletion is requested; however, snapshots are stored in-region for EU accounts unless the customer has enabled cross-region replication.

2) Proof-of-deletion: our standard report includes the request ids/session_ids submitted, job start and completion timestamps, the set of storage buckets/partitions affected (logical identifiers), and a machine-signed confirmation token. It does not include the deleted content itself.

3) Residency: for EU-scoped accounts (BrightBank will be configured as EU by default) both primary stores and automated snapshots remain within EU regions unless you explicitly request cross-region failover. We'll include that residency guarantee in the amendment.

Next steps:
- I'll have our Contracts team add a short paragraph to the MSA clarifying default TTLs and the EU snapshot residency guarantee.
- Marissa will provide a short proof-of-deletion template you can paste into your compliance ticketing system.
- If you want sub-24-hour erasure, we can scope an SLA and pricing proposal; Karhtik will follow up on that.

Would you like a 20-minute call Friday to finalize the language?

Thanks,
Jordan
